newsitem.title: NORWAY: Bullish blue chips push Oslo Bourse higher.
newsitem.headline: Bullish blue chips push Oslo Bourse higher.

text.p: Norwegian shares ended higher on Thursday led by blue chips after slipping for three days, but volume remained relatively modest.
Oslo's Total share index closed 0.8 percent higher at 1,174.44 points in turnover of 896 million crowns.
"Norwegian institutional investors have been the biggest buyers," one broker said, but added that most foreign investors were staying away from the Oslo Bourse.
The index kept climbing and received a late-session boost when U.S. figures showed a rise in weekly jobless claims and a narrower-than-expected international trade gap.
Anglo-Norwegian construction and engineering group Kvaerner was the most traded share at 107 million crowns, rising 2.29 percent to 424 crowns.
Industrial conglomerate Norsk Hydro rose 1.18 percent to 389 crowns in trade worth 71 million crowns.
Cruise company NCL jumped 5.56 percent to 23 crowns following the release of strong second-quarter profits by cruise group Carnival Corp of the United States, brokers said.
